fyNote: Financial year ends 30 June. FY2026 = July 2025 to June 2026 (audited). Next results: Q1 FY2027, due late November 2026.
segmentNote: A utilities group: Singapore power and UK water earn most of the money; data centres became a separate, fast-growing segment in FY2026 (AR p.21).

how.title: How YTL Power makes money
how.text: Revenue = electricity sold in Singapore + water and sewerage bills in the UK and Johor + data centre services + mobile subscriptions
facts: 298MW contracted; RM10.6bn invested so far (Q4 p.21)
To grow from GBP5.1bn to GBP7.3bn by 2030 (Q4 p.21)
215MW built of up to 500MW planned (Q4 p.21)

story.scale_label: revenue from power, water, data centres and telecoms

items.label: Cost of sales
items.tip: Fuel and gas for power plants, electricity bought, running the water network, staff and depreciation of plants and pipes.

items.label: Finance costs
items.tip: Interest on about RM40bn of borrowings.

items.label: Tax
items.tip: Tax in Singapore, the UK and Malaysia.

items.label: Profit to shareholders
items.tip: What is left for shareholders: paid as dividends or kept to grow the business.

pnl.incomeNote: Plus about RM2.82 per RM100 of revenue from other income and associates.

fiveYear.note: Dividend per share (sen): 2022 4.5 · 2023 6.0 · 2024 7.0 · 2025 8.0 · 2026 8.0. FY2024 was boosted by unusually high Singapore electricity prices.

rows.name: Power generation (Singapore)
rows.tip: YTL PowerSeraya plants and Geneco retail; profit nearly halved as electricity margins normalised.

rows.name: Wessex Water (UK)
rows.tip: Water and sewerage in south-west England; profit more than tripled.

rows.name: Ranhill (Johor water)
rows.tip: Water supply and treatment in Johor.

rows.name: Investment holding
rows.tip: Investments, Ryt Bank stake and other activities.

rows.name: Data centres
rows.tip: YTL Green Data Center Park in Kulai; reported as its own segment for the first time.

segments.note: Profit before tax by segment (AR p.21). About 85% of revenue comes from overseas.

assets.label: Power plants, pipes, data centres and other property
Money owed by customers and others

balance.note: Utilities borrow heavily against steady, regulated income: borrowings of RM39.9bn are almost double shareholders' funds. Cash fell from RM12.2bn to RM8.6bn as data-centre and plant spending continued (AR p.177-178).

waterfall.l: Power plants, data centres and networks
Stakes in associates and joint ventures

cash.wfNote: Operations produced RM2.4bn of cash, but spending on power plants, data centres and networks rose to RM7.6bn; new borrowing and the existing cash pile covered the gap, so cash fell by RM3.0bn.

metrics.label: Market value
metrics.plain: What the whole company costs at today's share price: RM37.8 billion.

metrics.label: P/E (FY2026)
metrics.plain: You pay about RM22 for every RM1 of yearly profit. A high number means investors expect growth.

metrics.label: EPS (FY2026)
metrics.plain: Profit earned for each share you own over the last year.

metrics.label: Dividend yield (FY2026 dividends)
metrics.plain: For every RM100 of shares, about RM1.8 a year comes back as cash dividends.

metrics.label: Payout ratio
metrics.plain: Of every RM100 profit, about RM41 is paid out; the rest is kept to grow.

metrics.label: Price to book
metrics.plain: The share price is 1.7 times the accounting value of what shareholders own.

metrics.label: Return on equity (FY2026)
metrics.plain: For every RM100 shareholders have in the company, it earned about RM8 profit last year.

metrics.label: Net margin FY2026
metrics.plain: What is left as profit for shareholders from every RM100 of revenue: RM7.66.

metrics.label: Revenue growth FY2026
metrics.plain: Revenue compared with the same period a year earlier.

metrics.label: Profit growth FY2026
metrics.plain: Profit to shareholders compared with the same period a year earlier.

metrics.label: Net debt
metrics.plain: Borrowings minus cash: RM31.24 billion owed to lenders after using all its cash.

metrics.label: Net gearing
metrics.plain: Net debt is 140% of shareholders' funds. Under 50% is usually seen as comfortable; above 100% means lenders fund more than owners.

metrics.label: Free cash flow FY2026
metrics.plain: Cash from operations minus spending on assets and land: RM-5,184 million. Negative means it borrowed or used savings to fund growth.

metrics.label: Free cash flow yield
metrics.plain: That spare cash as a share of the company's market value.

metrics.label: EV / EBITDA
metrics.plain: A price tag that includes debt: about 11.0 times its yearly cash earnings before interest and tax.

drivers.evidence: Power generation profit before tax fell from RM2.76bn to RM1.46bn (AR p.21)
drivers.why: The biggest earner is returning to normal after record years.

drivers.evidence: Wessex profit rose from RM166m to RM581m (AR p.21)
drivers.why: A regulated, steady business growing again.

drivers.evidence: The CMA's March 2026 final decision gave Wessex an improved outcome; its asset base is set to grow from GBP5.1bn to GBP7.3bn by 2030 (Q4 p.21)
drivers.why: Allowed returns grow with the asset base.

drivers.evidence: Ranhill profit rose from RM218m to RM312m (AR p.21)
Data-centre revenue rose from RM124m to RM867m and profit to RM347m; 298MW contracted (AR p.21; Q4 p.21)
drivers.why: A new growth engine riding AI demand.

drivers.evidence: 215MW of solar built, up to 500MW planned to co-power the park (Q4 p.21)
drivers.why: Cheaper, greener power for data-centre customers.

drivers.evidence: Telecommunications lost RM400m, up from RM256m (AR p.21)
drivers.why: A growing drag on group profit.

drivers.evidence: RM7.6bn spent on plants, data centres and property; cash fell to RM8.6bn (AR p.183, p.177)
drivers.why: Builds future income but stretches cash.

drivers.evidence: Borrowings of RM39.9bn vs shareholders' funds of RM22.1bn (AR p.178)
drivers.why: Normal for utilities, but sensitive to interest rates.

drivers.evidence: 600MW hydrogen-ready plant in Singapore due December 2027 (Q4 p.20)
drivers.why: Efficient new capacity, already secured despite a global turbine shortage.

drivers.evidence: Ryt Bank launched; ILMU AI models from YTL AI Labs (Q4 p.22)
drivers.why: Optional upside, but early-stage and costly.

drivers.evidence: Dividend kept at 8 sen per share (AR p.19)
About 22 times FY2026 profit at RM4.35 (see Valuation)
drivers.why: The price assumes data-centre growth will replace lower power profits.

suppliers: Fuel for the gas-fired power plants in Singapore; the main part of RM17.2bn cost of sales
Gas turbines (in global shortage) for the new 600MW hydrogen-ready plant
NVIDIA GPU systems for the YTL AI Cloud

RM39.9bn of borrowings, much of it backed by regulated water assets

Water and sewerage bills from Wessex Water, set by the UK regulator
298MW of the planned 1,200MW green data-centre park already contracted
supply.note: The report does not name its data-centre tenants or say what share of revenue any single customer provides.

competitors.source: General market knowledge, not the report

competitors.name: Data-centre developers in Johor
competitors.how: Compete for hyperscale and AI customers

outlook.text: Group performance expected to remain resilient given the essential nature of its businesses (Q4 p.22).
Wessex Water to deliver its 2025-30 investment plan after a supportive regulator decision; data-centre park to expand to 1,200MW (Q4 p.21).
Electricity demand in Singapore expected to remain stable (Q4 p.20).
Power profit has normalised from record levels and telecoms losses widened in FY2026 (AR p.21).

outlookOverall.text: Management expects resilient performance, with growth from water investment and data centres (Q4 p.21-22).
